subtitle: When Old Coins Outlived Fallen Kings

panels.shot: wide cinematic view of a bustling ancient port at dusk, half on land and half on sea
panels.action: Indo-Greek Merchant (Barygaza Route) stands on a crowded wharf of Barygaza, one hand holding a worn Greek drachma up to the fading light, behind him ships crowd the estuary and caravans snake inland.

dialogue.text: Long after Indo-Greek kings vanished, their drachmas still rang in Barygaza—how did dead rulers keep shaping the living sea roads?

i18n.hi: इंदो‑ग्रीक राजा ग़ायब हो गए, पर उनके दिरहम अभी भी भरोच में खनकते थे—मरे शासक ज़िंदा समुंदरी राहों को कैसे चलाते रहे?

panels.shot: slow push-in from the Indian Ocean toward the Gujarat coastline
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view shows the curve of the Gujarat coast, the gulf narrowing toward the estuary of Barygaza, with tiny sails like white seeds drifting toward the river mouth.

dialogue.text: To sailors from Egypt and Arabia, Barygaza was the hard-won prize at the end of a dangerous sea, where the land of India opened its grain stores, cotton bales and spices to the world.

i18n.hi: मिस्र और अरब के नाविकों के लिए भरोच ख़तरनाक समुंदर के बाद की कठिन मंज़िल थी, जहाँ भारत की धरती दुनिया के लिए अनाज, सूती गठरियाँ और मसाले खोल देती थी।

panels.shot: close-up on a rolled papyrus being unrolled on a ship deck
panels.action: Indo-Greek Merchant (Barygaza Route), older and weathered, leans over a Greek captain as they pore over a tattered scroll on a ship’s deck, the papyrus edges frayed from use.

dialogue.text: One anonymous sailor wrote a guide, the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, mapping winds, harbors and cargos; in its neat Greek lines, Barygaza looms large—a place of risk and reward.

i18n.hi: किसी अनजान नाविक ने एक गाइड लिखा—एरिथ्राई समुद्र का पेरिप्लस—जिसमें हवाएँ, बंदरगाह और माल दर्ज थे; उसकी सुघड़ यूनानी पंक्तियों में भरोच बड़ा, जोखिम और इनाम दोनों जैसा उभरता है।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a ship’s cramped cabin lit by an oil lamp
panels.action: The merchant runs his fingers over the Greek letters on the scroll, lips moving as he silently traces the section that describes the difficult approach to the harbor of Barygaza.

dialogue.text: The Periplus warns of Barygaza’s narrow, dangerous approach, the need for local pilots on the swirling estuary; yet it also whispers of firm rulers, busy markets and familiar coins.

i18n.hi: पेरिप्लस भरोच की तंग, खतरनाक घुसपैठ से सावधान करता है, बताता है कि घूमती खाड़ी में स्थानीय पायलट ज़रूरी हैं; फिर भी वहाँ सख़्त शासक, रौनक भरे बाज़ार और जानी‑पहचानी मुद्राएँ फुसफुसाकर दिखाता है।

panels.shot: transition shot showing a route map superimposed over caravan and sea scenes
panels.action: A stylized map-like view shows dotted lines from Egypt across the Red Sea to the Indian coast, then inland along the Narmada and northward toward Taxila, overlaid atop caravans and ships in motion.

dialogue.text: Long before Roman ships dared these waters, Indo-Greek rulers had learned the inland roads—taxing caravans between Bactria, Gandhara, the Indus delta and India’s western plains.

i18n.hi: रोमी जहाज़ों के इन पानी में घुसने से बहुत पहले, इंदो‑ग्रीक शासक अंदरूनी रास्तों को साध चुके थे—बैक्ट्रिया, गांधार, सिंधु डेल्टा और भारत के पश्चिमी मैदानों के कारवाँ से कर लेते हुए।

panels.shot: low-angle shot in a Gandharan marketplace
panels.action: In a Gandharan town, the merchant stands at a stall as a local money-changer weighs bilingual Indo-Greek coins on a small balance, stone Buddhist railings and Hellenistic-style pillars visible behind.

dialogue.text: In those northern cities, their kings struck a new kind of money—Greek legends on one side, Kharosthi on the other—coins that spoke to caravan men from many tongues at once.

i18n.hi: उन उत्तरी नगरों में उनके राजाओं ने सिक्कों की नई क़िस्म ढाली—एक तरफ यूनानी लेख, दूसरी तरफ खरोष्ठी—ऐसे सिक्के जो कारवाँ वालों को कई ज़बानों में एक साथ पुकारते थे।

panels.shot: tight close-up on a coin between finger and thumb
panels.action: The Indo-Greek Merchant holds up a silver drachma of Menander, its Greek inscription and figure of the king clear on one face, faint Kharosthi letters visible on the rim.

dialogue.text: Each drachma carried more than silver; it carried trust. Names like Menander and Apollodotus travelled with the coins, even when their armies did not.

i18n.hi: हर दिरहम में सिर्फ़ चाँदी नहीं, भरोसा भी ढला था। मेनандр और अपोल्लोडोतुस जैसे नाम सिक्कों के साथ चलते रहे, भले उनकी फ़ौजें न चलीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a caravan crossing a dry plain, camera tracking alongside
panels.action: A long camel caravan moves south across the dusty plains of western India, the merchant riding near the middle, sacks of coins and bales of cotton slung over the animals.

dialogue.text: From Taxila and the Indus towns, caravans pressed south and east, through Sindh and the dry tracts of western India, their loads a mix of cloth, spices, gems—and bags of Greek-style silver.

i18n.hi: तक्षशिला और सिंधु के नगरों से कारवाँ दक्षिण और पूरब को दबाते चले—सिंध, फिर पश्चिमी भारत की सूखी ज़मीनें—कपड़ा, मसाले, रत्न और यूनानी ढंग की चाँदी की थैलियाँ ढोते हुए।

panels.shot: overhead view of a bustling inland market on the Narmada route
panels.action: The merchant stands in a crowded inland bazaar beside the Narmada, surrounded by Indian traders, local rulers’ agents, and money-changers with trays of mixed coins—punch-marked, Indo-Greek, and local imitations.

dialogue.text: Political banners changed with each kingdom, but coins crossed frontiers as easily as caravans; local rulers accepted, copied or overstruck foreign pieces that suited their weights and trade.

i18n.hi: राजनीतिक झंडे हर राज के साथ बदले, मगर सिक्के सीमाएँ ऐसे पार करते रहे जैसे कारवाँ; स्थानीय राजाओं ने जो तौल और व्यापार में जमे, उन विदेशी सिक्कों को मान लिया, नकल की या उन पर अपने निशान चढ़ा दिए।

panels.shot: medium shot at a coin-dealer’s stall in Barygaza
panels.action: Now in Barygaza, the merchant leans over a stall where an Indian money-changer spreads out old, worn drachmas of Apollodotus and Menander alongside newer issues, all sorted in neat piles.

dialogue.text: When the Periplus writer reached Barygaza generations later, he still met these coins—old drachmas of Apollodotus and Menander, worn smooth from use, yet passing from hand to hand.

i18n.hi: पीढ़ियाँ बीतने पर जब पेरिप्लस का लेखक भरोच पहुँचा, तो उसे ये पुराने सिक्के अब भी मिले—अपोल्लोडोतुस और मेनандр के घिसे‑पिटे दिरहम, घिसावट के बावजूद हाथ से हाथ घूमते हुए।

panels.shot: close-up on the money-changer’s face and hands
panels.action: The money-changer, a local Indian merchant with a shrewd calm expression, weighs a Greek drachma on a small scale, eyes narrowing as he judges its silver content.

dialogue.speaker: indo_greek_merchants
dialogue.text: Menander’s name fades, friend, but his silver still holds, does it not?

i18n.hi: मेनандр का नाम धुंधला पड़ता है, दोस्त, पर उसकी चाँदी तो अब भी ठोस है, है न?

panels.shot: medium shot of dockside warehouses and customs officials
panels.action: On the riverside, the Indo-Greek Merchant stands before Indian officials at the entrance to large timber warehouses, his crates of goods open for inspection while scribes tally duties on palm leaves.

dialogue.text: The Periplus praises Barygaza’s rulers as strict but fair: customs charges fixed, officials exacting, yet the flow of goods ensured—an inland power managing a sea-gate once touched by Greek ventures.

i18n.hi: पेरिप्लस भरोच के शासकों को सख़्त पर न्यायी कहता है—शुल्क तय, अफ़सर कड़क, पर माल का बहाव पक्का—एक अंदरूनी ताकत जो उस समुद्री फाटक को चलाती थी जहाँ कभी यूनानी क़दम पहुँचे थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of inner harbor crowded with different ship types
panels.action: The inner harbor shows Egyptian-style sewn ships, Arabian craft and Indian vessels moored together, the Indo-Greek Merchant walking along the quay between bales marked with foreign symbols.

dialogue.text: Here, Egyptian and Arabian hulls lay alongside Indian boats; the same silver pieces that once paid soldiers in Gandhara now paid freight to the Gulf and to the Red Sea.

i18n.hi: यहीं मिस्री और अरब जहाज़ भारतीय नावों के साथ लगते थे; वही चाँदी जो कभी गांधार में सिपाहियों को मिलती थी, अब खाड़ी और लाल सागर तक भाड़ा चुकाती थी।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot in a merchant house at Barygaza
panels.action: Inside a merchant’s house, the Indo-Greek Merchant sits at a low table with Indian partners, a wax tablet and stylus before him, small stacks of mixed coins spread out as they calculate profits.

dialogue.text: Trade here did not require Indo-Greek governors. It used their legacies: shared weights, trusted coins, and routes once guarded by their garrisons, now policed by others yet still in use.

i18n.hi: यहाँ के सौदे को इंदो‑ग्रीक हाकिम नहीं चाहिए थे। यह उनकी छोड़ी विरासत पर चलता था—साझा बाट, भरोसेमंद सिक्के और वे राहें जिन्हें कभी उनकी चौकियाँ देखती थीं, अब औरों के पहरे में, पर अब भी ज़िंदा।

panels.shot: split-panel style composition, half showing a fading Indo-Greek fortress, half the busy Barygaza
panels.action: On one side, a ruined northern fortress with crumbling Hellenistic walls; on the other, the thriving Barygaza harbor with merchants exchanging old drachmas, the Indo-Greek Merchant bridging the two scenes.

dialogue.text: While stones of northern forts fell and dynasties changed, the economic lines they once defended stayed alive, carried by coins and memory, adapted to new masters and new markets.

i18n.hi: जब उत्तर के क़िले ढहे और राजवंश बदले, तब भी वे आर्थिक लकीरें जिंदा रहीं जिनकी वे रखवाली करते थे—सिक्कों और यादों के सहारे, नए मालिकों और नए बाज़ारों के हिसाब से ढलकर।

panels.shot: close-up on the Periplus scroll being annotated
panels.action: The merchant sits by lamplight aboard ship, adding small marks to the margin of the Periplus scroll as waves rock the hull, a few old drachmas lying beside the lamp.

dialogue.text: Our sailor-author notes simply that old Greek coins were current here. He does not claim Greek rule in Gujarat; he records circulation, not empire—an honest merchant’s eye for what truly mattered.

i18n.hi: हमारा नाविक‑लेखक बस इतना दर्ज करता है कि यहाँ पुराने यूनानी सिक्के चलन में थे। वह गुजरात में यूनानी राज का दावा नहीं करता; वह चलन दर्ज करता है, साम्राज्य नहीं—सच्चे सौदागर की नज़र से कि सच में क्या मायने रखता है।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of the merchant standing on deck at dawn, sea and sky vast
panels.action: At dawn, the Indo-Greek Merchant stands at the prow of the ship leaving Barygaza, the sea stretching before him as he turns a single drachma between his fingers, the shore a thin line behind.

dialogue.speaker: indo_greek_merchants
dialogue.text: Kings fall like waves on sand. But the routes we cut… endure.

i18n.hi: राजा रेत पर टूटती लहरों की तरह गिरते हैं। पर जो राहें हम काट जाते हैं… वे बनी रहती हैं।

panels.shot: wide historical montage shot fading from ancient to later traders
panels.action: A montage shows time passing: the Indo-Greek Merchant fades into later Indian and foreign traders on the same wharf, each handling old-style coins and newer issues, while the harbor of Barygaza subtly changes.

dialogue.text: Centuries rolled on. Indo-Greek names blurred, but the habits they helped shape—bilingual coins, shared measures, the threading of inland roads to ocean harbors—became part of the larger Indian Ocean world.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ बीतीं। इंदो‑ग्रीक नाम धुँधले हो गए, पर आदतें जो उन्होंने गढ़ने में मदद की—द्विभाषी सिक्के, साझा माप, और अंदरूनी सड़कों को समुंदरी बंदरगाहों से पिरोना—बड़े हिंद महासागर संसार का हिस्सा बन गईं।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on a modern archaeologist’s gloved hand holding an Indo-Greek coin in a trench, echoing earlier shots
panels.action: In a faintly indicated modern dig, gloved hands lift a corroded Indo-Greek drachma from the soil near an old trade route, its design barely visible, the gesture mirroring the ancient merchant’s earlier pose.

dialogue.text: Today, when we find their coins far from any Indo-Greek capital, we see how trade can outlast flags and fortresses: silent silver proof that the paths of merchants can outlive the kings who once guarded them.

i18n.hi: आज जब हम उनके सिक्के किसी भी इंदो‑ग्रीक राजधानी से दूर पाते हैं, तो दिखता है कि व्यापार झंडों और किलों से ज़्यादा टिकता है—ख़ामोश चाँदी की गवाही कि सौदागरों की राहें उन राजाओं से भी लंबी चलती हैं जो कभी उनकी रखवाली करते थे।

title_i18n.hi: भरोच के सौदागर और यूनानी दिरहम

subtitle_i18n.en: When Old Coins Outlived Fallen Kings
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब पुराने सिक्के डूबे राजाओं से भी लंबा जिए
